1. Who we are and what these terms cover

No Guesswork Events (“the app”) is an event-planning web app made by No Guesswork Systems LLC. These terms apply to everyone who uses it:

  • Hosts — the person planning an event, signed in or not.
  • Guests — someone who opens an invitation link and replies.
  • Vendors — a caterer, venue, photographer, or other supplier who opens a vendor-brief link a host shared.

Our Privacy Policy (what we collect and who sees it) and Refund Policy (the One-Event Pass) are part of these terms. Where they say something more specific about their subject, they control.

2. Eligibility

You must be at least 18 to create an account or buy the pass. The app is built for adults planning events; it has no age check, so this is a promise you make by using it.

Guests replying to an invitation do not create an account. A host may record a child's name and needs on a guest list; that is the host's data about their guest (section 6).

3. Accounts and sign-in

  • You can use the app without an account. Plans made while signed out live only in that browser's storage on that device.
  • Signing in is by email. We send a sign-in link and code to the address you give; use either one. There is no password. A bot check from Cloudflare runs on the sign-in form first.
  • Keep your email account secure. Anyone who can read that inbox can sign in as you. You are responsible for what happens under your account, and you should tell us promptly at events@noguessworksystems.com if you think someone else has used it.
  • Studios. Signed-in plans belong to a studio; database rules let only that studio's members read or change them. If you share a studio with someone, they can see and change its events.

4. The free tier and the One-Event Pass

What is free

Planning is free. Your first event of your own — a local, single-day event — is free to plan end to end: budgets, guests, timeline, every vendor tracked, the day itself, and one complete vendor-brief loop. Budgets, guests, timelines, and reading anything are never behind the pass on any event. Sample events are for exploring and never use up the free event.

What the pass is

The One-Event Pass is a single, one-time purchase that unlocks the paid parts of planning for one event. An event needs the pass for any of these:

  1. sharing vendor briefs with more than one vendor on that event;
  2. a destination or multi-day event (where everyone stays, getting there, getting around, the multi-day program);
  3. any event after your first one of your own.

Whichever reason applies, one pass unlocks that whole event. Whether an event needs the pass is decided once, when you create it, and the app tells you then. An event that started free stays free even if you later make it multi-day or a destination.

A vendor you have already shared a brief with can always keep viewing, receiving updates to, and confirming that brief; only sharing with a new vendor can need the pass.

What the pass is not

  • Not a subscription. It is charged once, through checkout you complete yourself. Nothing renews and nothing is charged again.
  • Not transferable. It belongs to the event it was bought for and cannot be moved to another event or another person.
  • Not bought twice. If an event already has a recorded purchase, checkout is refused rather than charging you again.
  • Not something a vendor pays for. Vendors are never charged a fee.

Price, payment, and taxes

  • The price is set by us, shown in the app before you buy, and charged in US dollars. It is fixed on our server; neither the app nor you can change it at checkout. Today it is $39.
  • We may change the price for future purchases. A change never affects a pass you already bought.
  • Payment is taken by Stripe on its hosted checkout page. We never see or store your card number.
  • Taxes: No sales tax is added to the $39 at checkout. The price shown in the app is the whole amount you are charged.
  • Preview period. While billing is switched off, every event is fully unlocked and nothing is charged; the app says so on the pass sheet and tells you before that changes.

5. Refunds, disputes, and revocation

Refunds are governed by the Refund Policy: a full refund within 14 days of purchase, no questions asked, as long as no new vendor brief has been sent from that event since the purchase.

What happens mechanically:

  • A full refund ends the pass. The event returns to the free tier; nothing you planned is deleted.
  • A partial refund keeps the pass.
  • A card dispute (chargeback) suspends the pass as soon as Stripe tells us about it. If the dispute is later resolved in our favor, access is not restored automatically; write to us.
  • Buying again after a refund or dispute goes through support, not checkout: the app refuses a second purchase on an event with a recorded one.

6. Hosts: your responsibilities for other people's information

Planning an event means entering information about other people. When you do, you are the one collecting it, and you are responsible for having the right to.

  • Guests. You may type or import guest names and record their dietary needs and allergies; guests may also give their own when they reply. Dietary and access needs can be health information. Enter only what you need to host people safely, and use it only for that.
  • Vendors. You may enter vendor names, contacts, and notes. Your private notes on a vendor are never shown to that vendor.
  • Email sent for you. When you ask the app to send an invitation, vendor message, or approval request, it is sent through our email provider on your behalf, to the addresses you chose. Send only to people who expect to hear from you about the event.
  • Invite links are keys. An invitation link carries a long random code, and that code is the only thing standing between the invitation and anyone who holds it. Anyone with the link can open the invitation — which shows the event's public details, including the venue address — and reply. Share it with the people you are inviting. One invitation accepts at most 500 distinct replies by default.
  • Shared studios. Anyone you add to your studio can see and change its events, including guest details.

7. Vendor-brief links

  • A vendor brief is a link a host shares with one vendor. It shows a fixed, limited slice of the plan: the vendor's own details and the host's note to them, the event's name, date, and venue, and that vendor's part of the run of show — never guests' details, money, contracts, or other vendors.
  • It is live. The brief is rebuilt from the host's current plan every time it is opened, so a vendor always sees the latest version.
  • It stays on until it is switched off by us. There is no button in the app to switch a brief link off yet. A host who needs a link stopped can write to us. Deleting your account switches off every brief link on its events.
  • Vendors do not need an account and are never charged. A vendor can confirm the booking or report a problem through the link, and we store that answer for the host.
  • The free tier includes one vendor-brief loop per free event; more vendors take the pass (section 4).

8. Acceptable use

Do not use the app to:

  • enter or share personal information about someone you have no right to share;
  • send invitations or messages to people who have not asked to hear from you, or to harass anyone;
  • submit false replies to an invitation, or flood an invitation or brief link with automated requests (both are rate-limited and capped);
  • try to reach another studio's events, guess invitation or brief codes, or get around the database rules that keep studios apart;
  • get around the pass, or resell, sublicense, or frame the app;
  • upload anything unlawful, or anything you do not have the right to upload;
  • misuse the AI drafting features. They run on prompts our server writes; you cannot send a free-form prompt, and they are rate-limited.

9. Your content, and the license you give us

  • Your plans are yours. You keep whatever rights you have in the plans, lists, notes, photos, and documents you put into the app (“your content”).
  • The license you give us is only what we need to run the app for you: to store, copy, display, and transmit your content, and to send it to the services the Privacy Policy lists (each sees only what its row says), for as long as it is in the app.
  • We do not sell your data or use it for advertising.
  • AI-drafted text (an event brief, a vendor follow-up, a summary of a document) is generated by a third-party AI model from the parts of your plan that feature needs. It can be wrong. Check it against the original before you rely on it or send it.
  • Feedback. If you send us suggestions, we may use them without owing you anything.
  • The app is ours. The software, the name “No Guesswork Events,” and the design belong to No Guesswork Systems LLC. These terms do not give you any right to them beyond using the app.

10. Availability and no warranty

The app is run by a small company on third-party services — hosting (Render), database and sign-in (Supabase), payments (Stripe), email (Resend), and others in the Privacy Policy. We work to keep it running and your data safe, but we do not promise it will always be available, error-free, or that nothing will ever be lost. Keep your own copy of anything you cannot afford to lose, such as vendor contracts and guest contact details.

Readiness scores, reminders, forecasts, cost estimates, and food-safety notes are planning aids drawn from what you entered and from public reference data. They are not professional advice and do not replace your own judgment, your vendors' instructions, or a guest's word about their own allergy.

To the fullest extent the law allows, the app is provided “as is” and “as available,” without warranties of any kind, express or implied, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement.

To the fullest extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or for lost profits, lost data, or a missed or disrupted event, arising from the app. Our total liability for any claim is limited to the greater of what you paid us in the 12 months before the claim or $100.

12. Ending your use, and deleting your account

You can stop at any time. Nothing renews, so there is nothing to cancel.

You can delete your account yourself, in the app: You & settings → Your account → Delete my account…, then type DELETE to confirm. You can also ask us at events@noguessworksystems.com.

Deleting your account permanently removes, at once:

  • your sign-in identity;
  • the events that belong only to you, with their guest lists, guests' replies, vendor-brief links and vendors' confirmations, and messages;
  • studios that only you belong to, your memberships, and invitations you sent;
  • the files you uploaded to those events.
  • on that device, the app's copies of the account's events. Plans that were only ever saved on the device stay there until you remove them.

It is not undone. Some things are kept, and the app says so before you confirm:

  • payment receipts for any pass you bought — with the link to your account removed;
  • security and administrative records;
  • content in a studio you share with others, which stays with your collaborators.

Deletion will stop and tell you what to do first if you are the only owner of a studio other people still use (make someone else an owner), or if you uploaded files to an event someone else still has (transfer or remove them).

We may suspend or end your access if you break these terms or the law, or if we stop offering the app. If we shut the app down, or suspend it for everyone, we will tell you at least 30 days before, and we will refund the pass for any event that has not yet been held.

Sections 6, 9 (feedback and our ownership), 10, 11, 13, and 14 survive the end of your use.
